summary: Final update, validated (valid; effect: interpretation append for question 0757162a, changing rationale, counterevidence and limitations). It closes the last item the account still carried as a loose consequence: what happens to a zero-length command batch downstream. Reading the captured executor path shows the batch is applied by a loop bounded by len(w.Cmds), so a COMMITTED instance with a non-nil zero-length command list applies nothing and writes no reply, yet is still marked EXECUTED and has ExecedUpTo advanced over it, and no guard on that path routes it back to recovery - executeCommands only diverts instances that are absent, below COMMITTED or nil-command (epaxos/epaxos.go:398-404), executeCommand admits COMMITTED instances (epaxos/exec.go:24-30), and strongconnect rejects only a nil slice (epaxos/exec.go:76-78). The rationale now names those anchors, separates the two independent causes of the missing client reply (the reply write sits inside the per-command loop; the re-offer guard needs exactly one NONE command), and records that the instance neither stalls its row nor re-enters recovery while instances queued behind it become executable. The limitation and counterevidence say plainly that this is a source derivation rather than an executed observation - no run drove the executor - while the measured client-side facts stand separately. That was the final open item in the account: six questions all explained, four asserted recovery-value defects and one refuted reachability claim on executed receipts, one holding client-completion contract, all statements, conditions, pointers and citations mutually consistent, and the captured source tree unmodified.
